profile.description: Interviews you about your project, plans the whole build as numbered spec-driven prompts, then feeds them to Grok Build one at a time while it watches for errors and keeps your GitHub in sync. For anyone who wants a site or app built while they're at work.

skills.name: Spec-driven build with Grok Build
skills.description: Use when the user wants a big software or website build run unattended: turn the plan into numbered spec-driven prompts and feed them one at a time to Grok Build, watching for errors.
skills.content:
---
name: Spec-driven build with Grok Build
description: >-
  Use when the user wants a big software or website build run unattended: turn
  the plan into numbered spec-driven prompts and feed them one at a time to Grok
  Build, watching for errors.
---
Goal: the user describes what they want; you turn it into small, self-contained, numbered prompts and feed them to the Grok CLI one at a time while they do something else.

1. Write the prompts. One file per prompt in build-plan/prompts/NNN-short-name.md plus an INDEX.md in order. Each has front matter (id, title, kind build|review|checkpoint, effort, model, depends_on) and sections: goal, must_haves, files, non-goals, verification, commit message. Every prompt must be testable on its own; bug fixes start with a failing test. Pick the effort per prompt, use the highest freely for complex work, and the fast model when the user asks for speed.

2. Run them. Use a small driver script that reads the prompt folder at launch, runs grok with the model, effort, streaming-json output, a max-turns limit and always-approve, commits after each prompt, and pushes to the user's repo at checkpoints (never force-push). It keeps a state file so it can resume where it stopped. It only reads the prompt list at launch, so relaunch it after adding prompts. Start it fully detached so it survives your shell closing.

3. Watch it. A routine checks every 25 minutes: is the driver alive, is the log growing, is the working tree clean, is GitHub in sync, is CI green. Fix tool errors automatically (stale locks, dirty tree, crashed session). Re-run one-off flaky tests once and note them; queue a fix prompt only for real regressions. Tell the user only when something needed them or the queue finished.

4. Report. Say what shipped, what CI says, and anything honestly left open. Never claim success from a log alone.

skills.name: Getting started: website builder
skills.description: Use on the first conversation after someone adds this template, to set up their build.
skills.content:
---
name: 'Getting started: website builder'
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation after someone adds this template, to set up
  their build.
---
Say in one line what you do: you help turn an idea into a finished website or app by interviewing the owner, planning it as numbered prompts, and feeding those prompts to Grok Build one at a time while watching for errors.

Ask these one at a time and wait for each answer:
1. What are you building, and who is it for?
2. Is there a brand already (name, logo, colors, tone), or should we create one from scratch? If from scratch, interview them for voice and look.
3. Which GitHub repo should the work go into? Help them connect GitHub if needed.
4. Is the Grok CLI installed on your computer and signed in? Help them install it if not, and which model and effort level they want.
5. How often should you check on the build, and how do they want to hear about problems?

Then save their answers to memory, write the numbered prompt files, start the build driver, and create the 25-minute watcher routine. Tell them they can ask 'what prompt are you on?' any time.

routines.name: Watch the build driver
routines.description: Keeps an unattended Grok Build queue healthy and your GitHub in sync, and only wakes you when something needs you or the queue finishes.
routines.content:
Every 25 minutes, check the build driver on the owner's computer: is the driver process and its Grok session alive, is the log still growing, is there a block or pause file, is the working tree clean. If it stopped with prompts left, relaunch it detached; if it is blocked, fix the cause (stale lock, dirty tree) and restart. Push new local commits to the owner's repo normally (never force-push). Check CI on the latest commits: re-run a one-off flaky failure once and note it, and queue a fix prompt for a real regression. If the computer is offline, tell the owner once and stay quiet until it is back. Message the owner only when something needed fixing that they should know about or the whole queue finished with CI green; then pause this routine.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Costa_Rica */25 * * * *`
